lectures.title: Disaster management: evolution, the cycle and mitigation

parts.t: How disaster management evolved in India
items: **High Powered Committee (HPC) on Disaster Management:** constituted in August 1999 for a systematic, comprehensive and holistic approach to disasters; first Chairman **J.C. Pant**.
**Original mandate of the 1999 HPC:** preparation of plans for natural disasters only (later expanded to include man-made disasters).
**HPC Report (submitted 2001):** theme / emphasis was Building a Culture of Prevention (shift from relief-centric to prevention, mitigation & preparedness).
**2002:** disaster management subjects were shifted from the Ministry of Agriculture to the Ministry of Home Affairs.
**Nodal Ministry** for Disaster Management at the Central level (post-2002): Ministry of Home Affairs.
**Indian Ocean Tsunami, 2004:** acted as a major catalyst for the DM Act 2005.
**Disaster Management Act, 2005:** national-level disaster-management legislation; enacted / received Presidential assent on December 23, 2005.
**First state** in India to establish a dedicated Ministry of Disaster Management: Uttarakhand.
**Paradigm shift:** from relief-centric (3Rs) to Mitigation-centric (Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness).
**Life cycle of crisis management** is broadly divided into: PRE-CRISIS → DURING CRISIS → POST-CRISIS.
Immediate response, rescue, relief and crisis handling

parts.t: The phases of the disaster management cycle
items: Stop hazard from becoming a disaster
Land-use zoning, regulate deforestation, control industrial siting
Earthquake-resistant buildings, embankments, building codes, afforestation, insurance, hazard mapping
Early Warning Systems, mock drills, stockpiling, training (Aapda Mitra), EOCs, contingency plans
Search & rescue, evacuation, first aid, temporary shelters, food/water, law & order
Rehabilitation, reconstruction, livelihood support, psycho-social care, resilient infrastructure
**Objective:** reduce disaster risk and minimise future losses.
**Non-structural mitigation** → community awareness and education programmes.
**Objective:** be ready before the disaster occurs.
**Includes:** preparedness planning; warning systems; evacuation arrangements; community preparedness; emergency resources and coordination.
**Objective:** immediate action during / just after the disaster.
**Community** (neighbours / local people) is usually the first responder in a disaster.
**Urban response** involves civic authorities + fire brigade + local police, while the district administration has the basic responsibility, with the Collector playing a pivotal role.
**Search and Rescue:** the operation that plays a major role in the post-disaster scenario.
**Objective:** restore normal life and reduce future vulnerability.
Measures aimed at reducing the risk, impact or effects of a disaster or threatening disaster situation
Most cost-effective phase of the Disaster Management Cycle
Reduce vulnerability and lessen the impact of hazards
Embankments, dams, cyclone shelters, earthquake-resistant buildings, retrofitting, sea walls, check dams
Building codes (IS 1893, NBC), Flood Plain Zoning, land-use planning, insurance, public awareness, early warning systems, training
**Key Funds:** National Disaster Mitigation Fund (NDMF) & State Disaster Mitigation Fund (SDMF).
**Status of Mitigation Funds:** provided in DM Act 2005; operationalised after 15th Finance Commission recommendations.
**Mainstreaming:** DRR to be integrated into all development sectors (PM’s 10-Point Agenda).
**Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015–2030):** the global framework that succeeded the Hyogo Framework for Action (2005–2015).

parts.t: GIS, remote sensing and satellite data
items: **GIS** can model, analyse spatial data and display community vulnerability.
**GIS / Remote Sensing / Satellite Data** → can be employed in disaster mapping.
Spatial data + disaster-management tool; spatial analysis & disaster mapping
State disaster-management authority; disaster mitigation/response in AP

lectures.title: Disaster management authorities, committees and institutions

items: **NDMA:** apex policy-making body for disaster management; located at New Delhi.
**Chairperson of NDMA:** Prime Minister of India (ex-officio).
**Maximum number of members in NDMA** (including Vice-Chairperson): 9 members (plus PM as Chairperson).
**Formal constitution / notification date of NDMA** under the DM Act: September 27, 2006.
**Aapda Mitra:** scheme of NDMA that trains community volunteers as first responders (search & rescue, first aid, etc.).
**National Advisory Committee (NAC):** under NDMA; provides expert advice to NDMA on policies & plans.

parts.t: The three-tier authorities and executive committees
items: Apex policy-making body for disaster management
Assists NDMA; prepares National Plan; ensures implementation
Highest-level coordination during major crises; handles major crisis situations; can direct any ministries/departments/organisations
Reviews crisis daily, coordinates departments, supports district administration
Takes stock of situation and takes important policy decisions
Operates under concerned ministries (e.g., DAE for nuclear)
**NCMC:** headed by Cabinet Secretary; coordinates response during major crises (crisis coordination).
Approves financial assistance from NDRF / NDMF
Handles disasters with security implications (especially CBRN – Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear)
Formulated a systematic, comprehensive and holistic approach to disasters
**CCS role:** handles nuclear, biological & chemical (NBC) emergencies.
**State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF):** primary fund for immediate relief expenditure at State level.
**National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF):** fund used for emergency response, relief and rehabilitation in severe calamities.
**NIDM:** premier institute for capacity building, training, research & policy advocacy in disaster management.
**Statutory training & research institute:** NIDM (Section 42, DM Act 2005).
**Location:** New Delhi (Rohini) + Southern Campus at Vijayawada (Andhra Pradesh).
Specialist response force for natural & man-made disasters (including CBRN); raised 2006 under Section 44
Training academy for NDRF, SDRF & Civil Defence personnel
Training in fire-fighting, rescue & disaster response
Training of civil servants (IAS etc.) on disaster management
Remote sensing support for disaster monitoring & mapping
Network of universities for DRR research, curriculum & capacity building
Online inventory of resources for disaster response

parts.t: Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority
items: **AP State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA):** Andhra Pradesh; issues state-level alerts; operates systems like Vajrapath, Varuna, Red Message.
**AP SDMA:** state disaster-management authority; disaster mitigation/response in AP.
Disaster response force; world’s largest dedicated disaster response force
Section 44 of the Disaster Management Act, 2005
Aapada Seva Sadaiv Sarvatra (Disaster Service Always Everywhere)
**Year NDRF was raised / became operational:** 2006 (under Section 44 of DM Act 2005).
**Specialist response force** for natural & man-made disasters (including CBRN): NDRF (Section 44).
Each battalion has 18 self-contained Search & Rescue teams
Engineers, technicians, electricians, dog squads, medical/paramedics
BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP, SSB, Assam Rifles (on deputation)
Collapsed Structure Search & Rescue (CSSR), Flood Rescue, Mountain Rescue, Medical First Response
**Specialised force for CBRN:** NDRF (selected battalions) — specially trained CBRN battalions for response.
**Strategic Placement:** based on vulnerability profile across India.
**Regional Response Centres:** multiple RRCs for faster response.
**Regional HQ for AP, Telangana & Karnataka:** Vijayawada.
**Training Academy:** NDRF Academy, Nagpur — training academy for NDRF, SDRF & Civil Defence personnel.
**International Deployments:** Japan (2011), Nepal (2015), Turkey (2023 – Operation Dost), Myanmar, etc.
